tool_input.description: Test agent construction end to end

result.result:
Iteration 13 is recorded. Summary:

## What I found (lineage analysis)

The lineage is a linear chain whose tip (`stripped-template-ranking`, b6060a9, **0.5511**) sits on a plateau: USPTO 0.18, Symptom2Disease 0.88, LawBench 0.59. I measured the losses across all 13 recorded runs (3380 samples) and most are not harness-reachable: LawBench's ~40 wrong samples/run have targets in no memory answer; USPTO's failures are RDKit-canonical SMILES writing (no offline canonicalizer); Symptom2Disease's memory delivers every val answer and the model still misdiagnoses. The `check_answer` tool has no measurable effect (47% correct when called vs 48% when not), and three prior ranking changes moved nothing.

The one clean, quantified defect: **the memory reached the solver only through a tool call the solver could skip.** `retrieve_examples` takes no arguments and returns a string `build_tools` computes from the question before the agent exists — a pure formality. 80 of 3380 samples never called it, **every one recorded with `memory_context_chars` 0** (no memory at all), 78 in a single model call, scoring **7/80 against 1895/3300** for the samples that read the memory (USPTO 7/73 vs 134/707; the parent's own run has two, both wrong).

## The change (`memory-in-prompt`, commit 52a532f)

The memory travels with the question: `build_tools` returns the listing itself, `solver.md` gains a `{memory}` slot, `render_prompt` writes question + steps + memory into one prompt, `retrieve_examples` is deleted, and the skill's step 1 no longer instructs a call. Since the listing is in the prompt, `Attempts` now builds the reduced-listing attempt's prompt along with its agent (`with_prompt`). Sized offline against the parent: byte-identical memory text on USPTO/Symptom2Disease (plus a charge-budgeted heading), 103.8 vs 103.7 examples on LawBench with an identical answer list.

## The result: void

**The evaluation failed at the provider, not at the harness.** All 260 samples died with `invalid_request` — the upstream message is Aliyun's `Access denied ... #overdue-payment` (the DashScope account is in arrears), 0 input/output tokens across the run, and the runner's own classifier calls it non-retryable and stopped. Preparation of the same tree completed normally, and the committed tree (`f83d88b2`) is exactly the evaluated tree.

I did **not** re-run: the runner keys a result to the source tree and short-circuits on any saved summary whose `rankable` is true, so this tree can never be re-measured — and a re-run would have required a doctored tree (a different candidate) and left a bogus 0.0 node in the lineage. The commit carries `evaluation_result` as the runner's void JSON with the failure described, and the note records the offline sizing, the failure, and that the expected effect is unobserved rather than disproved.
